title: Loop, tempo and click
learned: LOOP repeats the part between the START and STOP flags: work on one part at a time
Notes are stored in beats, so a song keeps its shape at any tempo
CLICK is a metronome; REC records a MIDI keyboard into the selected track
Space pauses and plays on; Space twice stops and goes back to bar 1

steps.why: A song is long, but you work on it a few bars at a time. The transport decides what plays: where, how fast and how often.
steps.do: Track 1 holds a four-bar melody and it is playing. Press F4 to open the Editor.
steps.after: The playhead runs through the song and on past its end into silence: without a loop the song just goes on.

steps.why: LOOP keeps the playhead inside a part.
steps.do: Turn LOOP on (the rounded rectangle in the transport bar at the bottom).
steps.after: In the ruler, the START and STOP flags mark the loop: bars 1 to 4, the whole melody. The playhead jumps back from STOP to START.

steps.why: A shorter loop lets you listen to one phrase over and over.
steps.do: Drag the STOP flag (lower half of the ruler) to the left, to bar 3.
steps.after: Only bars 1 and 2 repeat now. The flags snap to the grid; the loop is at least 1/16 long.
steps.try: Drag the START flag to bar 2 too, then put both flags back around bars 1 to 4.

steps.why: The tempo is the speed of the beat, in beats per minute (BPM).
steps.do: In the transport bar, drag the tempo display (120) upward to 140 or more.
steps.after: The melody plays faster but keeps its shape: notes are stored in beats, not seconds. Clocks synced to the transport follow the same tempo.
steps.try: Drag the tempo down below 100: the same melody becomes calm.

steps.why: To play along or record, you need to hear the beat.
steps.do: Turn CLICK on (the metronome button in the transport bar).
steps.after: A click on every beat, a higher one on the first beat of each bar. The number next to the tempo is the time signature: how many beats a bar has.
steps.try: With a MIDI keyboard: select a track, turn REC on and press Space. What you play is recorded into the track (one Ctrl+Z removes the whole take); Q tidies it up.

steps.why: Pause and stop are not the same.
steps.after: Two presses stop and take the playhead back to bar 1; a single Space only pauses, and the next Space plays on from where it stood.

steps.do: Loop, tempo, click, pause and stop: the transport serves the song. Press Space to play again, then Esc and Next to finish.
